title: The guide from fundamentals to computational practice on Neurogenomics
text:
By Aura Aguilar-Roldán
Welcome to blog. Below is the comprehensive guide and syllabus outlining the foundational and computational topics explored in this blog.
1. Introduction to the Field
1.1 Defining Neurogenomics
1.2 The Historical Context
1.3 Key Terminology & Glossary
2. Foundational Genetics and Genomic Architecture

DNA, RNA, and Protein Synthesis: A brief refresher on the central dogma.
Genetic Variation: Understanding SNPs, indels, and structural variants in the context of the nervous system.
Genomic Architecture: How the spatial organisation of the genome influences neurological function.

3. Computational Methods and Data Analysis

Introduction to the Bioinformatics Toolkit: Setting up your environment (R, Python, Bash).
Handling Large-Scale Genomic Datasets: Best practices for quality control and preprocessing.
Genome-Wide Association Studies (GWAS): Principles, execution, and interpreting Manhattan plots.
Transcriptomics (RNA-Seq): Analysing gene expression in brain tissue.

4. Complex Traits and Genetic Liabilities

Polygenic Risk Scores (PRS): Calculating and interpreting cumulative genetic risk for neurological conditions.
Exploring Genetic Liabilities: How subtle genetic variations contribute to complex brain disorders and behavioural traits.
Epigenetics and the Brain: How environmental factors influence gene expression without altering the DNA sequence.

5. Locus-Specific Studies and Applications

Deep Dives into Critical Regions: Unpacking the significance of highly associated regions (e.g., the MAPT locus) in neurodegeneration.
The Genetics of Sleep and Circadian Rhythms: How our DNA dictates our rest.
Pharmacogenomics: Tailoring neurological and psychiatric treatments based on individual genetic profiles.

6. The Future of Computational Neurogenomics

Single-Cell Sequencing: Mapping the brain one cell at a time.
Machine Learning Integration: Predictive modelling in genomic research.
Ethical Considerations: Data privacy, genetic testing, and the implications of neurogenomic profiling.

title: A Comprehensive Roadmap to Computational Neurogenomics
text:
Phase 1: Core Biological Foundations
Before analysing high-dimensional genomic datasets, one must master the unique cellular and molecular complexity of the central nervous system (CNS).

1.1. Molecular Neurobiology & Cellular Diversity

Characterisation of major CNS cell types: neurones, astrocytes, microglia, oligodendrocytes, and endothelial cells.
Synaptic plasticity, neurotransmission, and activity-dependent transcriptional programmes.

1.2. Genomic Architecture in the Brain

Structural variations, copy number variations (CNVs), and repeat expansions in neurobiology.
Somatic mosaicism: how genomic variation arises within single neurones during development and ageing.

1.3. Neuro-epigenetics & Gene Regulation

DNA methylation patterns and post-translational histone modifications in neural tissue.
Chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq) and 3D genome conformation (Hi-C) across neurodevelopmental trajectories.

title: A Comprehensive Roadmap to Computational Neurogenomics
text:
Phase 2: Essential Computational & Bioinformatic Toolkit
Rigorous computational neurogenomics relies on reproducible workflows and robust statistical modelling.

2.1. The Command-Line Environment & HPC

Navigating UNIX/Linux environments, Bash scripting, and job scheduling on High-Performance Computing (HPC) clusters (e.g., SLURM).

2.2. Programming Foundations for Biostatistical Modelling

R: Advanced data manipulation (tidyverse), genomic ranges (GenomicRanges), and statistical visualization (ggplot2).
Python: Scientific computing (numpy, scipy, pandas) and machine learning pipelines (scikit-learn).

2.3. Reproducible Research Practice

Version control using Git and GitHub.
Dynamic documentation and scientific publishing with Quarto and Jupyter Notebooks.

title: A Comprehensive Roadmap to Computational Neurogenomics
section: Phase 3: Primary Data Modalities & Analytical Workflows
text:
Phase 3: Primary Data Modalities & Analytical Workflows
This core section covers the processing, quality control, and interpretation of key neurogenomic assays.

3.1. Genome-Wide Association Studies (GWAS)

Investigating genetic liability for complex neurodegenerative and psychiatric conditions.
Polygenic Risk Scores (PRS) and linkage disequilibrium (LD) score regression.

3.2. Transcriptomic Profiling of Neural Tissue

Bulk RNA-seq: Alignment, quantification, and differential expression analysis in complex tissue homogenates.
Single-Cell & Single-Nucleus RNA-seq (scRNA-seq / snRNA-seq): Resolving cellular heterogeneity in human post-mortem brain samples using tools such as Seurat and Scanpy.

3.3. Spatial Transcriptomics

Mapping gene expression directly onto anatomical brain slices and neuroanatomical atlases.

title: A Comprehensive Roadmap to Computational Neurogenomics
text:
Phase 4: Applied Neurogenomics & Disease Modelling
Translating raw data into actionable neurobiological insights regarding disease mechanisms.

4.1. Investigating Complex Loci & Structural Variants

Fine-mapping and prioritisation of causal variants within challenging genomic loci (e.g., dissecting the neurodegenerative MAPT region).

4.2. Functional Integration & QTL Mapping

Expression Quantitative Trait Loci (eQTLs) and Splicing Quantitative Trait Loci (sQTLs) in brain tissue.
Co-expression network analyses (e.g., WGCNA) to identify disease-associated modules.

4.3. Multi-Omics Data Integration

Synthesising genetic, transcriptomic, and proteomic layers to uncover pathways underlying cognitive function and neurological disorders.

title: A Comprehensive Roadmap to Computational Neurogenomics
text:
Phase 5: Open Science, Ethics, & Biobanking

5.1. Navigating Large-Scale Genomic Consortia

Leveraging public resources: UK Biobank, PsychENCODE, GTEx, and the Allen Brain Atlas.

5.2. Ethical Considerations in Neuropsychiatric Genomics

Data privacy, patient consent, and mitigating historical biases in genomic diversity.
